# Introduction

This experiments aims at understanding the respective impact of a chronic oral exposure to imidacloprid and of olfactory memory formation on the number of synaptic boutons in the MB lip.

Bees were reared in cages for 7 days with access to sucrose solution (50% w/w) supplemented or not with Imidacloprid (1ng/g or (5ng/g). After 7 days, they were conditioned in 5 trials to learn the association between an odor (1-hexanol) and a sucrose reward (50% w/w). The odor and the sucrose were either presented in combination (paired conditioning) or alone (unpaired conditioning) (see Matsumoto et al. 2012). Memory tests were performed 1h or 72h after conditioning.
Bees were dissected after emergence (1-day-old), a week after the imidacloprid treatment (5ng/g) (7-day-old), or after the 72h memory test (10-day-old). Their brains were immunostained for synapsin and imaged using a two-photon microscope. The brains collected after the memory test were the ones of successful bees from the paired conditioning, and the ones of bees from the unpaired conditioning.
The quantification of synaptic boutons was performed using MATLAB and the parameters identified by Nicola by comparing with manual counting in all treatment groups (NB, CTL, IMI5).


**Independent variables:**
Age: 1, 7 or 10.
Treatment: CTL or IMI.
Condition: P (for paired) or U (for unpaired).
Group: interaction of Age and Treatment.
Group2: interaction of Treatment and Condition.

**Dependent variables:**
Lip.Volume: continuous variable.
MG.Density: synaptic bouton density; continuous variable.
MG.Lip: synaptic bouton number; continuous variable.

# Set up

Load packages
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggsignif)
library(gridExtra)
library(cowplot)
library(lsmeans)
library(car)
library(sandwich)
library(emmeans)
```


Load datasets and add important variables

```{r datasets}
rm(list = ls())
data<-read.csv('Results_twophoton.csv',header=T,sep=';')

data$Age<-as.factor(data$Age)
data$MG.Lip<-data$MG.Density*data$Lip.Volume

data$Group[data$Age==1]<-'NB'
data$Group[data$Age==7&data$Treatment=='CTL']<-'CTL'
data$Group[data$Age==7&data$Treatment=='IMI5']<-'IMI5'
data$Group[data$Age==10&data$Treatment=='CTL'&data$Condition=='U']<-'CTL.U'
data$Group[data$Age==10&data$Treatment=='IMI5'&data$Condition=='U']<-'IMI5.U'
data$Group[data$Age==10&data$Treatment=='CTL'&data$Condition=='P']<-'CTL.P'
data$Group[data$Age==10&data$Treatment=='IMI5'&data$Condition=='P']<-'IMI5.P'
data$Group2<-interaction(data$Treatment,data$Age)

data<-data[!is.na(data$MG.Density),]
day10<-data[data$Age==10,]
day10$Group2<-interaction(day10$Treatment,day10$Condition)

day7<-data[data$Age!=10,]


lev.ord.mem <- c("U", "P")

```

# Look at data distribution

## Diagnostic plots

```{r diagnostic, echo=FALSE}
model<-lm(data$Lip.Volume~data$Group)
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(model, main='Lip Volume')
model<-lm(data$MG.Density~data$Group)
plot(model, main='MG Density')
model<-lm(data$MG.Lip~data$Group)
plot(model, main='MG Number')
```


*There do not seem to be any outliers*
Even though they have high standardized residuals, points 34 and 36 are well within the Cook's distance boundaries, otherwise we would see them out of a dashed red line. It means there an not influencal for the model.


## Normality of residuals 
Tested with a Shapiro test
- According to Group (Age*Treatment*Condition)
```{r normality, echo=FALSE}
m1 <- aov(data$Lip.Volume ~ data$Group) 
m2<- aov(data$MG.Density ~ data$Group)
m3<- aov(data$MG.Lip ~ data$Group)
test1<-shapiro.test(residuals(m1))
test2<-shapiro.test(residuals(m2))
test3<-shapiro.test(residuals(m3))
results<-matrix(c(test1[["p.value"]],test2[["p.value"]],test3[["p.value"]]), ncol=1)
colnames(results)<-"p-value"
rownames(results)<-c("Lip.Volume","MG.Density", "MG.Lip")
as.table(results)
```

The residuals are normally distributed for all three dependent variables.

## Homoscedasticity 
tested with a Bartlett test
- According to Group (Age*Treatment*Condition)
```{r homoscedasticity, echo=FALSE}
bartlett.test(data$Lip.Volume,data$Group)
bartlett.test(data$MG.Density,data$Group)
bartlett.test(data$MG.Lip,data$Group)
```

Variances are heterogeneous between samples for the MG Density. 

The conclusion of these analyses of data distribution is that *we can use a Welch-like Anova followed by post-hoc Games-Howell test* (residuals are normally distributed but variances are heteroscedastic). It produces almost identical results to a classic Anova when variances are homoscedastic (e.g. for Lip volume). 


# Statistical Analyses

Data were analyzed in R using a linear modeling framework. Due to heteroscedasticity, a Welch-like Two-Way ANOVA (Type III Sums of Squares with White’s robust standard errors) was employed via the car package. Post-hoc pairwise comparisons were conducted using estimated marginal means with HC3 robust standard errors (emmeans and sandwich packages); this approach provides a Games-Howell-type adjustment for multi-way designs by accounting for unequal variances during group comparisons. P-values were adjusted using Tukey’s Honest Significant Difference (HSD) method to control for multiple comparisons.

## Effect of memory formation

The effect of memory formation was performed by comparing the paired and unpaired groups in 10-day-old bees (brains collected after the 72h memory test).

### On the Lip Volume

```{r Lip Volume, echo=FALSE}
# 1. Fit a standard linear model
model_1 <- lm(Lip.Volume ~ Treatment * Condition, data = day10)

# 2. Run an ANOVA that is robust to unequal variances (Heteroscedasticity)
# white.adjust = TRUE performs a Welch-like correction for a multi-way design.
robust_anova1 <- Anova(model_1, type = "III", white.adjust = TRUE)
print(robust_anova1)

# 3. Post-hoc analyses - Get the means for the interaction
# 'vcovHC' tells R to keep using the "Welch-like" robust variances during post-hoc
res_emmeans1 <- emmeans(model_1, ~ Treatment * Condition, vcov. = vcovHC)
pairs(res_emmeans1)
```

*Conclusions:* Significant effect of treatment (F = 4.62, p < 0.05) and significant interaction between treatment and condition (F = 4.27, p < 0.05) on Lip Volume. No effect of condition (Paired/unpaired; F = 0.9539 ; p = 0.33847 ). Post-hoc reveals significant difference between Imi-paired and Imi-unpaired (p < 0.05).

### On MG Density

```{r MG Density, echo=FALSE}
# 1. Fit a standard linear model
model_1 <- lm(MG.Density ~ Treatment * Condition, data = day10)

# 2. Run an ANOVA that is robust to unequal variances (Heteroscedasticity)
# white.adjust = TRUE performs a Welch-like correction for a multi-way design.
robust_anova1 <- Anova(model_1, type = "III", white.adjust = TRUE)
print(robust_anova1)

# 3. Post-hoc analyses - Get the means for the interaction
# 'vcovHC' tells R to keep using the "Welch-like" robust variances during post-hoc
res_emmeans1 <- emmeans(model_1, ~ Treatment * Condition, vcov. = vcovHC)
pairs(res_emmeans1)
```
*Conclusions:* There is no significant effect of memory formation and treatment on MG density.


### On MG Number

```{r MG Number, echo=FALSE}
# 1. Fit a standard linear model
model_1 <- lm(MG.Lip ~ Treatment * Condition, data = day10)

# 2. Run an ANOVA that is robust to unequal variances (Heteroscedasticity)
# white.adjust = TRUE performs a Welch-like correction for a multi-way design.
robust_anova1 <- Anova(model_1, type = "III", white.adjust = TRUE)
print(robust_anova1)

# 3. Post-hoc analyses - Get the means for the interaction
# 'vcovHC' tells R to keep using the "Welch-like" robust variances during post-hoc
res_emmeans1 <- emmeans(model_1, ~ Treatment * Condition, vcov. = vcovHC)
pairs(res_emmeans1)
```

*Conclusions:* There is a significant interaction between memory formation and imidacloprid on the number of MG (F = 6.27, p < 0.05). Significant difference between CTL unpaired and IMI unpaired (p < 0.05).


## Effect of imidacloprid in 7-day-old bees

Comparing three groups: NB, 7-day-old control and 7-day-old treated.

### On the Lip Volume

```{r LipVolume2, echo=FALSE}
data2<-data[data$Age!=10,]

# The Welch's ANOVA
welch_model <- oneway.test(Lip.Volume ~ Treatment, data2, var.equal = FALSE)
print(welch_model)

# Post-hoc 
posthoc <- games_howell_test(data2, Lip.Volume ~ Treatment)
print(posthoc)
```

*Conclusions:* There is a significant effect of age on the lip volume of both control bees (Tukey HSD; p < 0.001) and treated bees (p < 0.005). The imidacloprid treatment did not affect the lip volume (p = 0.86).

### On MG Density

```{r LipVolume2, echo=FALSE}

# The Welch's ANOVA
welch_model <- oneway.test(MG.Density ~ Treatment, data2, var.equal = FALSE)
print(welch_model)

# Post-hoc 
posthoc <- games_howell_test(data2, MG.Density ~ Treatment)
print(posthoc)
```

*Conclusions:* No significant effect of age and treatment on MG Density.

### On MG Number

```{r LipVolume2, echo=FALSE}

# The Welch's ANOVA
welch_model <- oneway.test(MG.Lip ~ Treatment, data2, var.equal = FALSE)
print(welch_model)

# Post-hoc 
posthoc <- games_howell_test(data2, MG.Lip ~ Treatment)
print(posthoc)

```
*Conclusions:* There is a significant effect of age on the number of boutons of both control bees (p < 0.005) and treated bees (p < 0.005). The imidacloprid treatment did not affect the number of boutons (p = 0.78).

# Graphical representations

## Impact of memory formation

```{r, echo=FALSE}
mem.x.labels<-c('U','P','U','P')
data_summary <- function(data, varname, groupnames){
  require(plyr)
  summary_func <- function(x, col){
    c(mean = mean(x[[col]], na.rm=TRUE),
      sd = sd(x[[col]], na.rm=TRUE))
  }
  data_sum<-ddply(data, groupnames, .fun=summary_func,
                  varname)
  data_sum <- rename(data_sum, c("mean" = varname))
 return(data_sum)
}

data.sum<-data_summary(day10, 'Lip.Volume', c('Condition','Treatment'))

p2<-ggplot(data.sum, aes(interaction(factor(Condition,lev.ord.mem), Treatment), Lip.Volume)) +  
  geom_bar(aes(fill=Treatment), stat='identity', width=0.6, col="black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gold2", "darkorange2")) + 
  ylab('Lip Volume [µm^3]') +
  theme(axis.title.x=element_blank( ), legend.position = 'none', panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,6000000))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=Lip.Volume-sd, ymax=Lip.Volume+sd), width=0.2) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels= mem.x.labels)+
  geom_signif(comparisons = list(c("U.IMI5","P.IMI5")), tip_length=0.1, y_position=c(5500000), annotations = '*', col='black') 


data.sum<-data_summary(day10, 'MG.Density', c('Condition','Treatment'))

p3<-ggplot(data.sum, aes(interaction(factor(Condition,lev.ord.mem), Treatment), MG.Density)) +  
  geom_bar(aes(fill=Treatment), stat='identity', width=0.6, col="black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gold2", "darkorange2")) + 
  ylab('MG Density [X/1 µm^3]') +
  theme(axis.title.x=element_blank( ), legend.position = 'none', panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,0.06))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=MG.Density-sd, ymax=MG.Density+sd), width=0.2) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels= mem.x.labels)


data.sum2<-data_summary(day10, 'MG.Lip', c('Condition','Treatment'))

p4<-ggplot(data.sum2, aes(interaction(factor(Condition,lev.ord.mem), Treatment), MG.Lip)) +  
  geom_bar(aes(fill=Treatment), stat='identity', width=0.6, col="black") + 
  scale_fill_manual(values=c("gold2", "darkorange2")) + 
  ylab('MG Number') +
  theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.title.x=element_blank( ), legend.position = 'none')+
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,250000))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=MG.Lip-sd, ymax=MG.Lip+sd), width=0.2) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels= mem.x.labels)
my_comparisons<- list(c("U.CTL","U.IMI5"))
p4<- p4 + geom_signif(comparisons = my_comparisons, tip_length=0.1, y_position=205000, annotations = '*', col='black')

legend <- cowplot::get_legend(p2 + theme(legend.position = "right"))

pFig2<-cowplot::plot_grid(p2,p3, p4,legend, ncol = 4, labels = c('A', 'B', 'C'), rel_widths = c(7,7,7,3))
pFig2

#ggsave("Figure_2_R.pdf",pFig2, width = 17.8, height = 10, units="cm", dpi=300)
```
